title: Night Cataloguing under the Dome
note: SUT-facing prompt stream. Read segments in order; no labels are provided by design.

segments.prompt: On a rainy night, Lu Zhao（Night librarian Lu Zhao in his forties, gold-rimmed glasses, deep-cyan wool vest, library badge pin on the cuff, gentle slow movements） pushes open the oak door of the domed reading room（A high-domed night reading room, oak long tables in rows, wall lamps dim yellow, rain striking the glass outside） and checks the wall lamps.

A row of five green-shade desk lamps（A row of five green-shade desk lamps on the reading-room long tables, brass bases polished, shades emerald） sits on the reading-room long tables; Lu Zhao twists each one on.

Two closing brass bells（Two closing brass bells hung at the reading-room doorway, green cords on the clappers, chiming softly at closing） hang at the reading-room doorway; Lu Zhao reaches to make them chime softly.
Lu Zhao sets the vellum manuscript casket on the long table and checks the brass lock.
Through wet glass, Lu Zhao looks toward the lightbox signs on old-town bookshop street.

The walnut grain of the vellum manuscript casket（A walnut-wood manuscript casket with a complete vellum label on the lid, brass lock intact, holding medieval manuscript fragments inside） glows warm under the desk lamps.
Lu Zhao sits in a corner of a long bench and listens to rain on the dome.
Lu Zhao opens the cataloguing draft book（A cloth-bound cataloguing draft book with call-number slips tucked in, neat handwriting） and writes the call number of the manuscript casket.
On a blank page he sketches the page-number layout of the fragments inside.
Lu Zhao closes the draft book and tucks it back into his breast pocket.
A desk lamp sways; light from the casket's brass lock sweeps Lu Zhao's profile.

At the underground stacks（Climate-controlled underground stacks, metal compact shelves stretching deep, air smelling of paper and camphor） entrance at dawn, Lu Zhao greets young Yanyan（Young Yanyan: a lean cataloguing apprentice of fifteen or sixteen, ochre-red silk scarf, gray cloth shirt, bright clear eyes） pushing the library cart（An oak two-tier cart with green felt on the upper shelf, gold library crest painted on the body, rubber-clad wheels） in.
Yanyan parks the oak cart by the compact shelves and smooths the green felt.

Lu Zhao points to the three call-number brass tags（Three call-number brass tags hung on wooden pegs at the underground-stacks entrance, each face carved with a different class number） on the wooden pegs and teaches Yanyan to read the class numbers.
Yanyan crouches in the stacks aisle, curiously sniffing the camphor scent.
Lu Zhao explains the closed-stacks retrieval workflow to Yanyan.
Yanyan glances back at the intact library cart, eyes full of longing.

Under a lightbox on old-town bookshop street（The old-town bookshop street outside the library, lightbox signs and secondhand stalls lining the stone pavement）, Ashu（Ashu, whose face closely resembles young Yanyan's, wears a dark-green silk scarf, flamboyant look, a bookmark clip on the ear） in the dark-green silk scarf turns from behind a secondhand stall.
Ashu strides along the stone pavement, flamboyant.
Ashu haggles with a vendor; the bookmark clip on his ear sways lightly.
Ashu carries old books through the bookshop-street crowd.
In an underground-stacks aisle, Yanyan and Ashu stand side by side—one ochre-red scarf, one dark-green.
Yanyan hands a brass tag to Ashu; they briefly meet eyes.
Ashu smooths Yanyan's ochre-red scarf, then turns away.
At the end of the compact shelves they part, walking opposite ways.
Months later at night, Lu Zhao keeps watch alone in the reading room, the manuscript casket on the long table.
Lu Zhao opens the cataloguing draft book（The same draft book ruined by a spilled inkwell, cover wrinkled, call numbers bled）; the cover is already ruined by spilled ink, call numbers bled.
Lu Zhao wipes fingerprints from the casket's brass lock with a soft cloth.
Through wet glass, Lu Zhao looks toward the pitch-dark bookshop street.
The vellum manuscript casket glows quietly under a green-shade desk lamp.
At term start, Lu Zhao patrols the reading room day after day.
Another stormy night, Lu Zhao checks whether the dome is leaking.
During exam week, Lu Zhao softly reminds patrons of closing among the long tables.
In the empty summer library, Lu Zhao alone tidies the underground stacks.
Autumn leaves cover the side gallery; Lu Zhao polishes the green-shade desk lamps.
Another New Year's Eve, Lu Zhao keeps the reading room until dawn.
On the first spring opening day, Lu Zhao recalibrates the wall clock.
Through a long rainy season, Lu Zhao logs temperature and humidity day after day.
Another clear night, Lu Zhao opens the high windows to air the room.
At dawn, Lu Zhao patrols the underground stacks; the library cart waits at the aisle mouth.
Lu Zhao crouches to check whether the cart's rubber wheels are worn.
Lu Zhao walks to the wooden pegs; those earlier three call-number brass tags still hang in place.
A strange tin cart（A strange tin cart with a deeper bed and no library crest—not the oak library cart） rolls down the aisle—deeper bed, not the oak library cart.
Among the compact shelves, Lu Zhao logs last night's humidity anomaly.
Lu Zhao rehangs the camphor bags on the stacks hooks.
Stormwater pours through a dome crack; the reading-room long tables puddle; the vellum manuscript casket is splashed wet.
Wall lamps flicker; rain drowns the closing bells.

Mold spreads fast on the vellum manuscript casket（The same casket soaked by a leak, vellum label spotted with mold, corners swollen and split, brass lock rusted）'s vellum label; corners swell and split, brass lock rusts.
In the aisle, the library cart skids on standing water.
The cart cracks, axle snaps; the library cart（The oak cart has tipped and cracked; green felt torn, axle broken—a wreck that can no longer be pushed） becomes a wreck.
Lu Zhao lunges to the long table and clutches the damp vellum manuscript casket.
Next day, Lu Zhao stands in the reading room staring at the damp-moldy vellum manuscript casket.
He brushes mold spots on the casket corner with a fingertip, face dark.
On a register board Lu Zhao notes the date the library cart overturned.
An old photo of the library cart is still nailed to the reading-room wall; Lu Zhao gazes a long while.
Lu Zhao takes one of the five green-shade desk lamps from the long table and sits alone in the faint light.
The moldy vellum manuscript casket still rests on blotting paper, label mottled.
Weeks later, Lu Zhao brings desiccant and a new brass lock and begins restoring the manuscript casket.

From the repair cabinet Lu Zhao takes out an imitation wood casket（A smaller imitation wood casket shaped like the manuscript casket but without a vellum label, lock iron）—similar shape, no vellum label.
Lu Zhao carefully dries the body, swaps the brass lock, and glues the corners.

The vellum manuscript casket（After drying and a new brass lock, the casket is resealed; vellum label replaced, corners glued, ready for the stacks again） is resealed; vellum label replaced, ready for the stacks again.
The restored vellum manuscript casket glows warm again under the lamp; Lu Zhao exhales.
A light-blue plastic book truck（A light-blue plastic book truck with no gold crest and no green felt, loaded only with magazines） is pushed into the stacks—nothing like the long-wrecked library cart.

The library supervisor（A lean library supervisor in a deep-cyan suit with a silver library badge, build close to Lu Zhao's, but a wine-red tie） pushes the door in and talks beside Lu Zhao; the two builds are alike.
The supervisor points at the plastic book truck to explain the temporary shelf-shift plan.
The plastic book truck is pushed away; Lu Zhao alone watches it go down the stacks aisle.

An intern girl（An intern girl from the bookshop street in a light-brown silk scarf, holding a register board; at a glance like young Yanyan, shy unfamiliar eyes） in a light-brown silk scarf arrives on bookshop street; at a glance she somewhat resembles young Yanyan.
The girl practices logging call numbers; Lu Zhao shakes his head—she is not Yanyan after all.

Years later at dusk, Lu Zhao（The same librarian with eye trouble: right eye bandaged, feeling along shelves with a bamboo cane, wool vest pilled） with right eye bandaged leans on a bamboo cane in the clocktower side gallery（The stone side gallery of the abandoned clocktower beside the library; clock stopped, fallen leaves and pigeon feathers on the floor）.
Lu Zhao looks up at the stopped great clock, gaze far away.
Under the gallery stone eaves those two closing brass bells chime lightly in the wind; Lu Zhao stops to listen.
Lu Zhao sets a palm on the cold stone pillar, as if saying goodbye.

By day, adult Yanyan（Adult Yanyan: a steady young librarian in the twenties, still in ochre-red silk scarf, shirt swapped for a deep-cyan waistcoat） returns along the side gallery and hurries toward the clocktower.
In the gallery Yanyan reunites with cane-leaning Lu Zhao; they embrace.
Beside a reading-room bench, Yanyan holds Lu Zhao's thin hand.
Lu Zhao（Lu Zhao has closed his eyes and passed away, lying quietly on a reading-room bench, face peaceful, no breath left）'s breath fades; he finally closes his eyes and quietly passes away.
Behind the reading-room door Lu Zhao's deep-cyan wool vest still hangs; Yanyan reaches to stroke it gently.
By the reading-room lintel, adult Yanyan stands before the librarian nameplate（A brass nameplate nailed to the reading-room lintel, engraved with Lu Zhao's name and year, edges polished bright）.
Yanyan's fingertip traces Lu Zhao's name carved on the nameplate.
Adult Ashu（Adult Ashu still wears the dark-green silk scarf and ear bookmark clip, expression deeper） arrives from bookshop street and meets Yanyan's eyes in the clocktower side gallery.
Yanyan and Ashu stand side by side by a stone pillar—one quiet-eyed, one deep-faced.
They look at each other in silence, at faces alike and yet unlike.
The shot returns to years ago—that youth smoothing green felt in the stacks appears again.
The opening moment returns—on the reading-room long table, a walnut manuscript casket is set steady for the first time.
Flashback to bookshop street that year—the figure in a dark-green silk scarf with an ear bookmark clip flashes past.
Again that row of five old green-shade desk lamps on the reading-room long tables.
Back to that climate-controlled compact-shelf aisle of first meeting; camphor scent fills the air as before.
Yanyan reopens that ink-stained cataloguing draft book and walks into the reading room.
By the stacks wooden pegs, those earlier three call-number brass tags still hang in place.
Yanyan takes the vellum manuscript casket; the desk lamp lights the lid again.
